samples: This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit table, with a header line and one right-aligned row for each of -10, 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40 degrees Celsius. It also offers a reusable, side-effect-free conversion function (multiply by 9/5, add 32) that other modules can call, and the only permission the program needs is writing to the console. One caution: the conversion and its documented examples mix whole-number literals with a decimal value, and the cheat sheet says Renyi has no implicit number conversion, so the checker may reject those spots. Run the checker before relying on it.

This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit table to the console: a header line, then one row for each temperature from -10 to 40 degrees in steps of 10 (so -10, 0, 10, 20, 30, 40), with both columns right-aligned. It also exposes a reusable, pure conversion function that turns a Decimal Celsius value into Fahrenheit, and it documents that function with examples such as 0 giving 32 and -40 giving -40. It needs only console access, with no files, network, or other side effects, so it is safe to run, though the range and step are fixed in the code and cannot be configured.

This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion table to the console: a header line, then one row for each of -10, 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40 degrees Celsius, with the two columns right-aligned. It also provides a reusable, public function that converts a single Celsius temperature to Fahrenheit, which comes with examples covering the freezing point, the boiling point and the -40 crossover. It is pure computation plus console output, needs no other permissions (no files, network or the like), and has a fixed range with no input, so it suits a quick reference or demo but would need editing to change the range.
